record.title: API and worker images consume floating base tags, unpinned PyPI specs, and an unsigned rembg model
record.description: Each Docker rebuild of Dockerfile.api and Dockerfile.worker runs pip install against requirements.txt lower bounds and pulls python:3.12-slim-bookworm by tag. The API image additionally downloads the rembg u2netp model during build with no checksum. A PyPI or registry publisher who can change a matching version, retag the base image, or replace the rembg model bytes can land code or weights in the next Railway image. Web JS is lockfiled via npm ci; the Node base tag is still floating. Live resolved digests were not observed.
record.claimed_root_cause: Maintained Dockerfiles treat mutable tags and unbounded pip specs as the release input, and bake a remotely fetched rembg model into the API image without an integrity pin.

trace.description: API image starts from an unpinned rolling distro tag.
Runtime Python dependencies are specified only as >= versions, with no lockfile consumed by Docker.
Build runs pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt then rembg new_session('u2netp'), baking whatever those resolvers return into the image that later runs uvicorn.

evidence.description: Worker uses the same floating python:3.12-slim-bookworm tag and pip install -r requirements.txt without a rembg digest pin.
Web build and runtime use node:22-bookworm-slim by tag; npm ci plus package-lock.json pins JS packages only.
npm ci is the contrasting control: frontend lockfile is copied and used, unlike Python.
Production images are built from repository root using these Dockerfiles, or optionally Procfile/Nixpacks, on each git push.

record.reason: Source confirms the floating tags and unpinned pip path: infra/docker/Dockerfile.api:2 and Dockerfile.worker:4 FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm; Dockerfile.web:2 and :20 FROM node:22-bookworm-slim; requirements.txt uses >= lower bounds (bcrypt alone has <6); Dockerfile.api:10-11 RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt then rembg new_session('u2netp'); worker :12 installs the same file without prefetching the model. That is missing pin/digest hygiene, not a cross-boundary result. There is no lower-trust writer: resolvers use official image names and default PyPI (no extra-index-url, pip.conf, or alternate root), COPY only this repo's requirements.txt, and there is no in-repo CI, cache, or PR job a contributor could poison. The claimed actor is a generic publisher of packages already named in source. The consuming job is the owner's git-push Railway rebuild (DEPLOY.md:11, :194; same-principal). Dockerfile.web:4-5 already lockfiles JS via npm ci. Observing live Railway digests or hashing u2netp would only snapshot current floating resolution; it would not add a distinct writer or an unauthorized path into trusted output.
